title: Static Analysis
vs the AI Agents
title_card.subtitle: Parasoft C/C++test  |  SWE-sweep benchmark  |  MISRA / CERT

headline: If AI writes the code,
do we still need static analysis?
bullets: LLM agents find and fix bugs, but how many?
Safety critical industries need evidence, not impressions

headline: 488 real bugs,
14 C and C++ repositories
bullets: Byte-identical bug-era code, the project's own compile flags
Parasoft C/C++test: Flow Analysis + MISRA C 2025 / C++ 2023 + SEI CERT

headline: 41.4% on the bugs of its kind,
37.5% of all 488 vs 4.5% by agents
bullets: 183 of 488 bugs: a Parasoft finding inside the changed code
67 of the 162 mechanism bugs: 41.4%, clearing the 40% mark
Flow Analysis alone caught 16 bugs outright
Same code, same bugs, published benchmark

headline: What this benchmark
does not claim
bullets: Agents searched whole repositories; the analyzer got the buggy files
Most hits are coding standard rules, not proven root causes
Reproducible: full pipeline and configs on GitHub

headline: Only a third of the bugs
are static analysis's kind of bug
bullets: 162 of 488: memory, resource, and error handling defects
Parasoft on that third: 41.4%, clearing the 40% mark
24.7% on the exact defect line; robust at 38.8% to 41.4% across passes
The logic two thirds: review, requirements-based testing, coverage
